questions.title: Your character in the bed
questions.question: In a roleplay turn, what may Natalie write of your character's body during an explicit scene?
questions.context: Natalie never thinks, speaks or acts for your PC (player character; R49-01, R52-10). For fights you ruled 'wounds as world facts', with 'how he bears it' yours (R71-6). Yoko Mishiro, his canon wife, is an NPC Natalie voices, so the bed needs the same line drawn before it is needed.

options.label: His post, her answer
options.consequence: Natalie writes only the partner and the room; every act of his body, and every response in it, comes from your post, and the turn stops wherever his body would next move.

options.label: Contact as world fact
options.consequence: Once your post sets the act, contact, position and what the partner does to him are world facts; his arousal, pleasure, pain and climax, and how he bears them, stay yours.

options.label: B, plus the outward signs
options.consequence: As B, and what the partner can see or feel of him (hardness, breath, sweat, a flinch) is written as the partner registers it, R71-6's outward model; what he feels and when he comes stay yours.

questions.rec_reason: In a fight a wound is the world's doing; in bed his body's answer is his character, so contact runs as world fact while the response, seen or felt, waits on your post.

questions.title: The explicit roleplay turn
questions.question: How does a full roleplay turn run when the scene in it is explicit?
questions.context: Every reply is a full turn of about 3,500 words (R49-30), and every turn stops at your next decision (Table Rule 1); in bed the decisions come fast. For fights you allowed standing orders, conditions Natalie runs 'until the first branch they do not cover' (R71-5).

options.label: Partner and world fill it
options.consequence: The turn runs on the partner's side and the world beyond the door (the house, the watch, the weather) up to his next decision, half texture and talk, half the world moving (R49-29).

options.label: Standing orders in bed
options.consequence: You may post the course of the encounter, a pace, a limit or a stop for your character, and Natalie runs it to the first branch it does not cover, then stops there.

options.label: Short turns in bed
options.consequence: This reopens R49-30: an explicit turn may run short and stop at each decision, so the exchange moves at the speed of the act.

questions.rec_reason: It keeps your full-length turn and your character in your hands at once, the same answer you gave for fights; A's world beyond the door still fills what the orders leave.

questions.title: An NPC who would force him
questions.question: If an NPC would coerce or force your character, how far does the turn go?
questions.context: NPCs pursue their wants (Table Rule 3), and some will want to take what is not offered. In a fight an NPC's blow lands as world fact once your move resolves (R71-6). Coercion of a player's own character is where tables most need a clear line, and it covers guest players at the Discord table too.

options.label: Lands like a blow
options.consequence: The NPC's act is written as a world fact, as a wound would be; how he bears it is yours.

options.label: Threat placed, his post decides
options.consequence: Natalie sets the threat in the room (the grip, the bargain, the Draft in the cup) and stops; the act reaches the page only through your post.

options.label: Never against a PC
options.consequence: NPCs may want it and say so; no NPC forces or coerces a player's character on the page.

questions.rec_reason: It keeps Rule 3's dangerous NPC and Rule 1's stop at your decision together, and gives a guest player at the Discord table the same say you have.

settled.point: The floor: adults only, nothing sexual involving minors ever, no explicit sex on real living people, no bestiality. Canon treats adult beastkin as people who marry (Yoko Mishiro's card); an animal, a Well-spawn or a summoned creature is never a partner.
settled.why_not_asked: NATALIE.md's floor is fixed and never on a questionnaire; it is not a rule row. Every sample here is between adults.

settled.point: Table Rule 9's clauses: plain anatomical vocabulary, clinical specificity, positions tracked, arousal scents, onomatopoeia, the NPC's own desire and refusal line and change of mind, a consequence, dubcon and non-con at the same specificity, aftermath never skipped.
settled.why_not_asked: Standing law in NATALIE.md, extended by R70-133 and R70-134; K4, SC3 and SC11 ask only how its clauses are carried out.

settled.point: Explicit narration is plain and crude: working-man anatomical words, lush in sensation, blunt in naming.
settled.why_not_asked: Ruled 2026-09-26 and kept by the style law; SC1 asks only whose words.

settled.point: Which strand leads in bed: the POV's culture keys it (a Moto POV writes with image and the held detail, a Kharven POV blunt), the anatomy stays plain under every strand, and LitRPG reaches the bed only at a readout moment.
settled.why_not_asked: XS2 already answered which strand leads in bed, by the POV's culture; asking it again for every POV would have re-asked R70-134.

settled.point: Euphemism in explicit narration (his member, her sex, manhood) is out.
settled.why_not_asked: R49-51 is 'blunt in naming'. ME2 C asks only whether verify enforces it with a word list.

settled.point: Season imagery, the held detail at the peak, the poem after, and mimetic words romanised and never italic, all beside the plain words.
The techniques are keyed to the POV's culture; the lover's culture shows in what they do and say.
Your PC and the other creators' characters are never thought, voiced or acted for; you may voice any NPC, a lover included.
settled.why_not_asked: Standing law; SC12 to SC14 ask only where the line falls in bed.

settled.point: NPC thought: one italic thought per NPC in a roleplay turn, none under a written scene's POV lock, so a partner's desire shows through body and speech there.
settled.why_not_asked: Prose law, unchanged in bed.

settled.point: Third person only; roleplay turns in present tense, written scenes in past.
settled.why_not_asked: VO3 of the style law, and the prose law.

settled.point: The narrator never passes a moral verdict on what happens in bed; a verdict lives only in the POV's own idiom.
settled.why_not_asked: Standing anti-machine law; SC9 builds on it.

settled.point: Pop-psych words (boundaries, triggered, closure) stay out of narration; modern words, safeword and aftercare among them, are legal in speech and italic thought.
settled.why_not_asked: Vocabulary law; SC6 asks only how a game is framed in the world.

settled.point: Profanity in speech and close POV, each culture's own swears first.
settled.why_not_asked: Settled by the vocabulary law.

settled.point: Jo-ha-kyū tempo for set pieces and kishōtenketsu (set-up, development, twist, reconciliation) for quiet scenes reach explicit scenes as they reach any other.
settled.why_not_asked: SP1 and SP2 of the style law; nothing here reopens them.

settled.point: Feeling carried by one held image and never named; a scene may close on verse set apart.
settled.why_not_asked: IN3 and DT6 of the style law.

settled.point: A lover gets the full first-sight inventory in the POV's own order, and one changed detail on each return.
settled.why_not_asked: Description law applies to lovers as to anyone.

settled.point: Turns run about 3,500 words and set pieces 5,000 and up.
settled.why_not_asked: Prose law; SC2 and SC13 ask only how explicit scenes use those lengths.

settled.point: Every working costs something visible in the body, and no figure is invented.
settled.why_not_asked: Standing law; SC8 builds on it.

settled.point: Each culture's own sound and state words, entered in its Inventory and never italic.
settled.why_not_asked: RH4 of the style law; the bed draws on the same banks.

settled.point: NPCs lie, refuse and pursue their wants, and a betrayal is foreshadowed so a player could catch it.
settled.why_not_asked: Table Rules 3 and 8 and the play law; a lover is an NPC like any other.

settled.point: Medicine is true to place and purse.
settled.why_not_asked: World texture and combat law; K5 asks only what the Ledger keeps, and conception and the pox are CO11.

settled.point: Humour in bed: anyone may be funny inside the act, the joke arriving in progress and never as setup, deadpan and reaction; full comic beats belong to carded comic voices; inside danger, a coerced scene included, only gallows wit.
settled.why_not_asked: The humour law already reaches every scene, beds included.

settled.point: Readouts and Pressure in bed: a readout comes only at an appraisal, a wound line or Essence spent, never from Pressure and never with a joke in it; Pressure shows in the room first; holding it in costs the holder's jaw, collar and temper.
settled.why_not_asked: Style and combat law already answer it; whether Pressure can reach desire, and what a Stage gap costs a couple, are CO13 and CO12.
